A laboratory thermometer usually reads from \(-10^\circ\)C to \(110^\circ\)C. A clinical thermometer has the much smaller range of 35 °C to 42 °C.

value: Fossil fuels can be made in the laboratory (incorrect)
reasoning: Fossil fuels such as coal, petroleum and natural gas formed over millions of years from the dead remains of living things, so they are exhaustible. They cannot be made in a laboratory, so statement A is the incorrect one.
Depositing a layer of a desired metal on another material using electric current is called electroplating, for example chromium plating on taps and cycle parts.
At constant speed the object covers equal distances in equal times, so distance grows evenly with time and the distance-time graph is a straight line.
Animals that lay eggs, like frogs, lizards and hens, are called oviparous. Animals that give birth to young ones, like humans and cows, are viviparous.
The iris is the coloured part of the eye behind the cornea. Its colour gives each person's eye its distinctive colour; it also controls the size of the pupil.

Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of pulses (iv). Lactobacillus sets curd (iii). A protozoan (Plasmodium) causes malaria (i). A fungus causes rust of wheat (ii). So the match is A-iv, B-iii, C-i, D-ii.

First the fleece is cut off the sheep (shearing), then washed to remove grease and dirt (scouring), then separated by texture (sorting). Only after that are the fibres straightened, combed and rolled into yarn.
Micro-organisms decompose dead plants and animals into humus, the dark organic matter that makes soil fertile.
Speed is the distance covered in unit time, so \(\text{Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}}\).
Evaporation takes heat from the surroundings, so it causes cooling, not heating. That is why sweat drying on the skin cools us. The other three statements are true.
The number of oscillations a vibrating object makes per second is its frequency, measured in hertz (Hz).
Air is matter, so it does occupy space: a balloon swells as air fills it. The other statements are true, so D is the incorrect one.

value: A cylindrical magnet has only one pole (incorrect)
reasoning: Every magnet, whatever its shape, has two poles, north and south. So a cylindrical magnet cannot have only one pole. The other statements are correct.
Milk of magnesia is magnesium hydroxide, a mild base used as an antacid to neutralise extra acid in the stomach.

Opaque objects do not let light through (b). Transparent objects let light through so we can see clearly through them (c). Translucent objects let light through only partially (a).
In parasitism one organism benefits and the other is harmed (2). In commensalism one benefits and the other is not affected (3). In mutualism both benefit (1).
A concave mirror gives an enlarged, upright image when the object is close to it, so dentists use it to see magnified teeth.
Alveoli are tiny air sacs in the lungs surrounded by blood vessels. Oxygen passes from them into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out, so their job is the exchange of gases.
Bile, made by the liver and stored in the gall bladder, breaks fat into tiny droplets and so helps in the digestion of fats.
In a solid, heat passes from the hotter end to the colder end through the material itself. This is conduction. Convection happens in liquids and gases, and radiation needs no medium.
The Richter scale measures the strength (magnitude) of an earthquake.
The pistil is the female part of a flower: stigma, style and ovary, with ovules inside the ovary. The anther belongs to the stamen, the male part, so it is not part of the pistil.

value: The Shivaliks are the lowest ranges of the Himalayas
reasoning: The Shivaliks are the outermost and lowest range. The Himadri (Great Himalayas) is the highest and most rugged, with Mount Everest, and is too cold for much settlement. The Himachal is the middle range. So only B is correct.
A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. A hygrometer measures humidity, a thermometer measures temperature and an anemometer measures wind speed.
A plateau is raised land with a flat top and often steep sides. Plateaus are rich in minerals, which is why they are called storehouses of minerals.
The time difference is 9 pm minus 6 pm, which is 3 hours or 180 minutes. The Earth turns \(1^\circ\) every 4 minutes, so the difference in longitude is \(\frac{180}{4} = 45^\circ\).
The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920, not 1928. Quit India (1942), Civil Disobedience (1930) and Champaran (1917) are correctly dated.
The Lok Sabha has 543 elected members (C). The Rajya Sabha has 233 elected members (A) and 12 members nominated by the President (B).

On hill slopes, broad flat steps (terraces) are cut so that water cannot rush down and carry the soil away. Terrace farming is the usual soil conservation method in hilly areas.
The Gram Panchayat is the village-level body of local self-government. The Vidhan Sabha is the state legislature, and the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are the houses of Parliament.
Both the Union and the State governments can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List, such as education and forests. The Union List is for the Union alone and the State List for the states.
Lothal is in Gujarat. Ropar is in Punjab, Kalibangan is in Rajasthan, and Dholavira is in Gujarat, so the other three pairs are wrong.
The subsidiary alliance was brought in by Lord Wellesley in 1798, and the Nizam of Hyderabad was the first ruler to accept it.
The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) praising Samudragupta was composed by Harisena, his court poet.
Fa-Hien (Faxian) came to India around 400 CE, during the reign of the Gupta ruler Chandragupta II.
In the Lok Sabha, 47 constituencies are reserved for Scheduled Tribes. The figure 84 is the number reserved for Scheduled Castes.

Sustainable development means using resources wisely (A), balancing our needs with the need to conserve (C), and saving resources for future generations (D). Unlimited use of resources now (B) is the opposite of sustainable development.
The Thar, in Rajasthan and nearby areas, is a hot desert, the Great Indian Desert.

Sprinkler irrigation, drip irrigation and rainwater harvesting all save water. Agricultural runoff is water flowing off fields, often carrying fertilisers, so it wastes and pollutes water rather than conserving it.

The equator (\(0^\circ\) latitude) is the largest circle of latitude, so it is the longest. It lies in the hot (torrid) zone, not the frigid zone, and it is a parallel of latitude, not a longitude or meridian.

The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal was introduced in 1793 by Governor General Charles Cornwallis.
The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the East India Company under Robert Clive and Sirajuddaulah, the Nawab of Bengal.
Amuktamalyada, a Telugu poem, was written by Krishnadeva Raya, the famous ruler of the Vijayanagara empire.
